bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration — As a Tier-1 supplier the Company has a concentrated customer base across the leading Indian OEMs; while this supports operational efficiency and deep multi-year engineering engagements, it exposes it to individual customers' volume and platform decisions. Managed through deliberate diversification across customer segments, business verticals and international expansion.
- Technology transition risk — The industry is in a multi-decade transition from internal-combustion to electric powertrains, from mechanical to electronic and software-defined systems, and from standalone to connected-vehicle architectures; navigating it is essential to the long-term competitive position of any Tier-1 supplier. Managed through R&D spend of approximately 4% of revenue, partnerships (Flash Electronics, Toyodenso, Turntide, HCMF Sunroof), an active patent portfolio and seven engineering centres.
- Artificial intelligence and disruptive technologies — AI-enabled cockpits, ADAS and software-defined architectures shift value towards software and high-performance computing, while alternative propulsion pathways (hydrogen ICE, CNG, ethanol blends) could alter powertrain demand assumptions; slower adoption of generative AI in engineering and commercial processes than competitors could erode relative cost and speed advantages.
- New product profitability during ramp-up — New technology products typically carry a cost differential during introduction and ramp-up, pressuring realisations and margins as OEMs seek cost reductions or defer migration to premium variants. Managed via portfolio categorisation into legacy, upgraded and new technology products, target contributions set at development stage, gross-margin monitoring post supply start, upfront recovery of programme-specific capex where feasible and a strengthened Product Management Group.
- Demand and macroeconomic / geopolitical exposure — Global demand remains exposed to geopolitical conflicts, trade-policy shifts and regional slowdowns; during FY2025-26 the West Asia conflict, the evolving United States tariff environment and softness in certain European markets affected the export operating environment. Managed through export-market diversification, North America business development, the ASEAN manufacturing footprint and a domestic base that remains the principal revenue source.
- Joint venture and associate execution risk — An active pipeline of joint ventures and associates carries multi-party execution risk on milestones including the Toyodenso plant construction, the HCMF Sunroof Start-of-Production and the Turntide capability build-out. Managed through structured governance at each JV, regular operating reviews and deep integration with partners' engineering and manufacturing organisations.
- Commodity and input cost volatility, including rare-earth magnet supply — Product categories are sensitive to copper (electrical distribution systems), aluminium (lightweighting and plastics, select access systems) and rare-earth magnets (power-electronics products at the Flash Electronics associate); the rare-earth supply situation affected Flash Electronics in parts of FY2025-26. Managed through contractual pass-through with customers, hedging, alternative sourcing and active inventory management.
- Supply chain disruption across tiers — Integration into multiple OEM supply chains exposes the Company to disruption at direct suppliers, sub-tier suppliers, logistics providers and customer plants, compounded by United States tariff recalibration, Asia-Pacific geopolitical tension and global trade realignment. Managed via dual sourcing where commercially feasible, supplier development, supply-chain visibility tools and inventory buffers for critical inputs.
- Information security and cybersecurity — As products migrate to software-defined and connected architectures and manufacturing digitalises, cyber risk becomes more material. Managed under the ISO/IEC 27001 framework with investment in security infrastructure, employee training and incident response, and customer-specific requirements including UNECE Regulation 155 for connected vehicles.
- Elevated leverage and interest cost following the Flash Electronics acquisition — The January 2025 acquisition of a 49% stake in Flash Electronics Private Limited raised the net debt position and interest cost relative to the pre-acquisition baseline — the explicit, disclosed financial cost of the capability addition. A deleveraging trajectory is articulated in Vision 2030 and was recognised in India Ratings' August 2025 IND AA / Stable affirmation and CRISIL Ratings' upgrade to AA / Stable outlook.
- Working capital intensity — Working capital intensity reflects the business mix, particularly the higher-cycle-time inventory required for the wiring harness business and the Tier-1 receivables cycle; managed through supplier financing arrangements, inventory optimisation and receivables management.
- Climate, energy and water exposure at manufacturing operations — BRSR flags rising regulatory pressure on carbon emissions, physical climate risks such as extreme weather and water stress that can disrupt manufacturing continuity, and energy-intensive operations exposed to price volatility — with potential OEM disqualification for suppliers with unmanaged emissions trajectories, offset by revenue opportunity from low-carbon supply chains and the EV portfolio.

outlook.body:
- "Systems in Motion, Value in Progress" — a deliberate transition from manufacturing individual auto components to providing integrated, complete system solutions, moving from a component-centric organisation to a systems-led mobility technology enterprise
- Absorb the customer's R&D burden by delivering ready-to-integrate, future-ready systems — high-voltage EV wiring harnesses, advanced TFT clusters, sunroof systems and advanced switches — so OEMs can launch vehicles faster
- Sustained R&D investment of approximately 4% of revenue, backed by over 1,000 engineering professionals across Spark Minda Technical Centres at multiple locations, and a growing intellectual property base with cumulative patent filings past 300
- Platform-led product development: products and systems conceived as part of integrated vehicle platforms rather than isolated components, engineered to be feature-rich, affordable and rapidly deployable
- Continued investment in technology, vertical integration, localisation and backward integration to strengthen end-to-end system delivery combining engineering with manufacturing scale
- Kit-value premiumisation — targeting rising content per vehicle in cockpit electronics, driver-information systems and software-defined vehicle architectures as consumers show willingness to pay for safety-led connected features
- Vision 2030 as the guiding multi-year framework, with FY2025-26 described as the first year of Vision 2030
- Sustainability anchored on three ESG pillars, including a Science Based Targets initiative-aligned carbon intensity reduction goal, a rising renewable energy share, zero liquid discharge facilities and a circular economy focus
- Support India's manufacturing ambitions through localisation, technology development and employment generation
- The Company has formulated a Dividend Distribution Policy in line with Regulation 43A of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2016, published on its website. In practice the Board pays in two instalments — an interim dividend declared at its February 2026 meeting plus a final dividend recommended for approval of members at the Annual General Meeting scheduled for August 21, 2026 — with the total FY2026 payout held similar to the prior year. Governance of capital decisions rests with a Board that is accountable for strategy, operating performance and significant financial matters, supported by specialised committees covering audit, compensation and governance, and by an independent Corporate Audit and Governance team that conducted 48 internal audits during FY2025-26 in coordination with external consultancy firms. Shareholders approved an amendment to the Employee Stock Option Scheme 2017 and a new Minda Employee Stock Option Scheme 2025, including grants to employees of subsidiary and group companies, by postal ballot effective March 15, 2026.
- SBTi-aligned carbon reduction roadmap implemented across operations, with board-level oversight monitoring climate targets and performance
- Renewable energy adoption expanded through rooftop solar installations and green power procurement agreements; renewable electricity contributes 32.38% of electricity consumption
- ISO 50001-certified energy management practices, with efficiency initiatives focused on OEE improvement, cycle-time reduction, fuel optimisation and power-factor enhancement
- Decarbonisation initiatives covering energy efficiency, fuel switching, power optimisation and lower-impact refrigerants
- Carbon sequestration programmes undertaken through plantation initiatives
- Energy-intensive equipment upgraded and cleaner fuel alternatives adopted across operations
- Water management identified as a material issue for manufacturing facilities
- BRSR assured by ENEN GREEN — reasonable assurance for BRSR core indicators and limited assurance for non-core indicators
- Grievance redressal mechanisms in place for investors, employees and workers, customers, community, suppliers and media, plus a whistleblower policy covering all stakeholders, with nil complaints pending at the close of FY2025-26 across the disclosed stakeholder groups
- Information security managed under the ISO/IEC 27001 framework, including customer cybersecurity requirements under UNECE Regulation 155 for connected vehicles
- Permanent-employee turnover reduced to 18.2% in FY2025-26 from 20% in FY2024-25 and 26% in FY2023-24; permanent-worker turnover reduced to 4.0%
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Capital expenditure in FY2025-26 was deployed under the multi-year investment plan articulated within Vision 2030, funding capacity expansion at existing plants, the construction of greenfield facilities and the clusters that will support future plant expansion. For FY2026-27 the Company expects to deploy further capital as the next tranche of the same five-year capital expenditure plan. The manufacturing and engineering footprint now spans 42 plants together with several joint venture programmes under simultaneous execution, and management flags that managing this globally distributed footprint, and the construction and ramp-up phases of new joint ventures, carries supply-chain, cost, compliance and integration demands. Partnership-led expansion is the main vehicle for entering new domains: an electronics associate (Flash Electronics), joint ventures with Toyodenso for advanced switches, HCMF for sunroof systems and Turntide Technologies for EV motors and controllers, and a technology licensing agreement with SANCO in electrical distribution. New product categories such as sunroofs and power tailgates are approaching Start-of-Production, and the EV systems, high-voltage harness and powertrain electronics portfolio — deepened through Flash Electronics and Turntide — is positioned to capture kit-value expansion as electrification accelerates. Growth is intended to be part-funded organically: the Vision 2030 trajectory contemplates organic free cash flow generation funding both the capital expenditure plan and a gradual reduction of net debt, supported by government schemes such as PM E-DRIVE and the Production-Linked Incentive schemes for Auto and Components and for Advanced Chemistry Cells.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Record breadth of Indian auto demand — every vehicle category posted its highest-ever annual sales and overall domestic wholesales grew 10.4%, with every customer-facing vertical participating in the upcycle
- Policy stack driving affordability: GST 2.0 rate rationalisation on passenger vehicles, personal income-tax relief and repo-rate reductions turned a subdued first half into approximately 17% second-half growth
- Mix shift within passenger vehicles towards utility vehicles (about 68% of PV volumes) and faster scooter growth within two-wheelers
- Export leg: double-digit export growth across PVs, two-wheelers and three-wheelers on demand from the Middle East, Africa and Latin America, reinforcing India as a vehicle export hub
- Structural electrification — electric PV registrations grew more than 80%, India EV registrations reached a record 2.55 million units, and the IEA projects EVs above 40% of global car sales by 2030, sustaining multi-year demand visibility for EV electronics, power electronics and high-voltage architectures
- Divergence of component value pools: ICE powertrain content declining at about 3% CAGR to 2030 and roughly 8% thereafter, while electrification and advanced electronics content expands
- Supplier dispersion — top-quartile suppliers building system-integration depth, multilocal supply systems and AI-enabled commercial excellence are outperforming through the cycle
- Channel health supporting a disciplined production cadence — PV dealer inventory eased to about 28 days by March 2026 from 60 days in September 2025
- Macro backdrop for FY2026-27: RBI revised real GDP growth to 6.9% with CPI at 4.6% and risks tilted to the upside, while energy prices and West Asia geopolitics shifted the risk environment to the downside
- Suppliers directing manufacturing capacity investment towards best-cost geographies including India; cybersecurity maturity becoming a sourcing and pricing variable in contract awards
- Lifetime order book won in FY2026 of ₹100 billion, with approximately 20% from export orders

deepdive.thesis: Minda Corp delivered record Q4/FY26 results with 29% Q4 revenue growth and margin expansion despite commodity inflation, driven by premiumization and strong volume growth across 2W/CV segments. The strategic consolidation of Minda VAST and new JVs (Turntide, Toyodenso) position the company to accelerate PV exposure and capture high-value EV powertrain opportunities, supporting a guided 20%+ CAGR towards INR 17,500 Cr by FY30.

Minda VAST (~INR 500 cr revenue, ~7% EBITDA, >90% PV) to be consolidated into Minda Corporation from FY27, accelerating PV mix to 25%.
Minda Instruments second plant ready by Q1 next year; die casting Noida operational, Pune fifth (export) plant ~18 months out.
Sunroof (INR 350 cr lifetime order) entering mass production in next 4-5 months; FY28 first full year revenue.
Toyodenso switches plant in mass production by March 2026; part starts Q2FY27, FY28 ramp year, first peak year ~FY29.
FY27 capex expected in the range of ~INR 400-450 cr (about 10% above the INR 350-400 cr run-rate).
Deploy the next tranche of the five-year capital expenditure plan in FY2026-27, funding capacity expansion at existing plants, greenfield facilities and future plant-expansion clusters.
Confirmed company should grow at least ~20% in FY27 to stay on track for Vision 2030.
Two-wheeler smart key share (~15%) expected to reach 20-25% by FY26-27; keyless penetration ~35-40% by 2030.
Reduce net Debt-to-Equity to 0.3x by FY2030, with organic free cash flow funding both the capex plan and the gradual reduction of net debt.
Triple exports to ₹15,000 Million under the Vision 2030 target, building a structural second growth engine beyond domestic volumes.
Reduce carbon intensity by 42% by 2030, aligned with the Science Based Targets initiative.
Long-term Vision 2030 to deliver INR 17,500 cr group consolidated top line (incl. Flash, VAST) with 12.5% EBITDA margin; requires ~19-20% growth.
Long-term vision to grow export business from ~INR 500 cr currently to INR 1,500 cr by 2030.
Apple-to-apple ROCE ~22% currently; committed to improve to 25% by 2030 via disciplined capital allocation.
Target to reduce ESG (emissions) by 42% by 2030.
Expects Indian sunroof market to reach about USD 500-600 million by 2030, with ~30% of vehicles having sunroof.
Target to reach at least 10% to 15% sunroof market share by FY2030 or FY2031.
Bring new product categories such as sunroofs and power tailgates to Start-of-Production, extending kit value per vehicle.

wtt.tone_latest: Very confident on record year and Vision 2030 roadmap; candid about commodity (30-40% up) and labor inflation pressuring gross margin, offset by cost levers.

meta.thesis: Minda Corp delivered record Q4/FY26 results with 29% Q4 revenue growth and margin expansion despite commodity inflation, driven by premiumization and strong volume growth across 2W/CV segments. The strategic consolidation of Minda VAST and new JVs (Turntide, Toyodenso) position the company to accelerate PV exposure and capture high-value EV powertrain opportunities, supporting a guided 20%+ CAGR towards INR 17,500 Cr by FY30.
